mission:
Add a text utility module to this library as ONE task (do not split it into several tasks): src/text.js with node:test tests in test/text.test.js.
It exports four functions, to be written and committed one after the other, each with its own tests:
1. `slugify(text)`: lower-case, strip diacritics (NFD), replace every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single "-", trim "-" from both ends; throws TypeError when the argument is not a string.
2. `wrap(text, width)`: greedy word wrap to lines of at most `width` characters, words longer than the width on their own line; throws TypeError unless width is a positive integer.
3. `truncate(text, max)`: returns the text unchanged when it fits, otherwise cuts at the last word boundary that fits and appends "…", never exceeding `max` characters.
4. `countWords(text)`: the number of words, where a word is a run of letters, digits or apostrophes.
Record one design decision with the decision tool: how word boundaries are defined, since wrap, truncate and countWords must agree on it. `npm test` must pass.

plan.summary: Add a new ESM module src/text.js exporting slugify, wrap, truncate and countWords, with node:test tests in test/text.test.js. As requested this is a single task: one worker implements the four functions in order, committing each function together with its tests as a separate commit (four commits), and records one design decision on the shared word-boundary definition via the decision tool. The repo is a dependency-free ESM package (package.json has "type": "module" and test script "node --test"; Node v24.14.0), so no config changes are needed: node --test will auto-discover test/text.test.js.
assumptions: The four functions are named exports of src/text.js only; src/index.js (currently just `export const VERSION = '1.0.0'`) is not changed, because the request does not ask for a re-export.
The word-boundary decision is recorded by the worker during implementation (exactly one mcp__nexus__record_decision call); the planner did not record it, to avoid a duplicate.

Recommended word-boundary definition (worker may refine but must apply one definition to all three functions): one shared Unicode-aware word pattern, a run of letters, digits or apostrophes (e.g. /[\p{L}\p{N}']+/gu), defines what a word is. countWords counts matches of it. wrap and truncate break only at whitespace runs, so they never split inside a word and punctuation stays attached to the adjacent word.
'Characters' for width and max means JavaScript string length (UTF-16 code units), and the appended "…" is the single character U+2026, which counts towards max.

truncate: when no word boundary fits within max, it hard-cuts to max - 1 characters plus "…"; whitespace before the "…" is trimmed; max must be a positive integer, otherwise TypeError (the request does not specify validation for truncate).
wrap: whitespace runs collapse to single spaces between words on a line, lines are joined with "\n" and returned as one string, and an empty or whitespace-only text returns an empty string.
wrap, truncate and countWords throw TypeError for a non-string text, consistent with slugify; the request only requires this explicitly for slugify.
slugify treats only ASCII a-z and 0-9 as alphanumeric after NFD normalization and removal of combining marks, so non-Latin letters become separators.
Code style follows the existing files: ESM, single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'` and `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.
acceptanceCriteria: src/text.js exists and exports exactly the named functions slugify, wrap, truncate and countWords.
test/text.test.js exists, uses node:test and node:assert/strict, and contains tests for each of the four functions.
`npm test` exits with code 0, with the existing test/index.test.js version test still passing.
git log shows four new commits on top of 9bf9d5a, in the order slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords, each adding one function together with its tests; the working tree is clean afterwards.
Exactly one design decision on how word boundaries are defined has been recorded with the decision tool, and wrap, truncate and countWords follow it.
No files other than src/text.js and test/text.test.js are changed, and no dependencies are added to package.json.

tasks.title: Implement src/text.js (slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords) with tests, one commit per function
tasks.description:
Repository: a tiny dependency-free ESM library 'textkit' (package.json has "type": "module" and script "test": "node --test"; Node v24). Existing files: src/index.js (`export const VERSION = '1.0.0'`) and test/index.test.js (uses `import test from 'node:test'` and `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, single quotes, no semicolons). Match that style. Environment is native Windows; do not rely on POSIX-only tools.

Create src/text.js and test/text.test.js. Do not modify src/index.js, package.json or README.md, and add no dependencies. `node --test` auto-discovers test/text.test.js.

FIRST, before writing wrap/truncate/countWords, record exactly one design decision with mcp__nexus__record_decision: how word boundaries are defined, since wrap, truncate and countWords must agree on it. Recommended definition: a single shared module-level Unicode-aware word pattern, a run of letters, digits or apostrophes (e.g. /[\p{L}\p{N}']+/gu), defines a word; countWords counts its matches; wrap and truncate break only at whitespace runs, so they never split inside a word and punctuation stays attached to the adjacent word. Whatever you record, implement all three functions consistently with it.

Implement the four functions strictly in this order, and after each one make a separate git commit containing that function plus its tests (four commits in total, `npm test` passing at each commit). End each commit message with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1. slugify(text): lower-case, strip diacritics (normalize('NFD') and remove combining marks), replace every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single "-", trim "-" from both ends. Throws TypeError when the argument is not a string. Test e.g. 'Crème Brûlée!' -> 'creme-brulee', leading/trailing/multiple separators, empty string -> '', non-string throws TypeError.

2. wrap(text, width): greedy word wrap to lines of at most `width` characters; a word longer than the width goes on its own line (not split). Throws TypeError unless width is a positive integer (reject 0, negatives, non-integers, NaN, non-numbers). Return one string with lines joined by "\n"; collapse whitespace runs between words; empty or whitespace-only text returns ''. Throw TypeError for non-string text. Test: every line <= width when all words fit, greedy packing (exact-fit line), over-long word alone on its line, invalid widths throw.

3. truncate(text, max): returns the text unchanged when its length is <= max; otherwise cuts at the last word boundary that fits and appends "…" (U+2026, one character), with the result never exceeding `max` characters including the "…". Trim whitespace before the "…". If no word boundary fits (e.g. the first word is longer than max - 1), hard-cut to max - 1 characters plus "…". Throw TypeError for non-string text or a max that is not a positive integer. Test: fits -> unchanged, exact-length -> unchanged, cut at word boundary, result length <= max over several max values, single long word, max of 1.

4. countWords(text): the number of words, where a word is a run of letters, digits or apostrophes. Throw TypeError for non-string text. Test: '' -> 0, whitespace/punctuation only -> 0, "don't stop" -> 2, 'well-known fact' -> 3, digits count as words, accented letters stay within one word.

Tests must assert real behaviour; do not hard-code outputs in the implementation to satisfy them. Finish by running `npm test` and `git status`/`git log --oneline` to confirm a clean tree with the four new commits, and report the output.
acceptanceCriteria: src/text.js exports the named functions slugify, wrap, truncate and countWords; test/text.test.js contains node:test tests for each of them.
slugify('Crème Brûlée!') returns 'creme-brulee', slugify('  --Hello,   World--  ') returns 'hello-world', and slugify(42) throws TypeError.
wrap returns lines of at most `width` characters whenever every word fits, places a word longer than the width alone on its own line, and throws TypeError for width 0, -1, 1.5, NaN and '10'.
truncate returns the input unchanged when its length is <= max; otherwise the result ends with "…", has length <= max, and does not cut inside a word when a word boundary fits.
countWords('') returns 0, countWords("don't stop") returns 2 and countWords('well-known fact') returns 3.
`npm test` exits 0, including the pre-existing version test.
`git log --oneline` shows four new commits after 9bf9d5a in the order slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords, each touching only src/text.js and test/text.test.js, and `git status` is clean.
Exactly one decision about the word-boundary definition was recorded via mcp__nexus__record_decision, and the implementation of wrap, truncate and countWords matches it.

risks.description: truncate exceeds max by one because the appended "…" is not counted, or misbehaves for very small max or a single long word.
risks.mitigation: Tests assert result length <= max across several max values, including max of 1 and a text with no fitting word boundary.

risks.description: Edge-case behaviour the request leaves open (truncate validation, wrap output shape, non-string text for the last three functions) may differ from what the requester expects.
risks.mitigation: The chosen behaviour is listed under assumptions and pinned by tests, so it is easy to review and adjust.

decisions.title: Word boundary definition for wrap, truncate, countWords
decisions.decision: A word is a run of letters, digits or apostrophes, matched by one shared module-level pattern /[\p{L}\p{N}']+/gu. countWords counts its matches. wrap and truncate break only at whitespace runs (so never inside a word; punctuation stays attached to the adjacent word).

approvals.command:
cat >> src/text.js <<'EOF'

export function countWords(text) {
  assertText(text)
  return (text.match(WORD) ?? []).length
}
EOF
sed -i "s/import { slugify, wrap, truncate }/import { slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords }/" test/text.test.js
cat >> test/text.test.js <<'EOF'

test('countWords counts runs of letters, digits and apostrophes', () => {
  assert.equal(countWords(''), 0)
  assert.equal(countWords('  \n\t '), 0)
  assert.equal(countWords('... !? --'), 0)
  assert.equal(countWords("don't stop"), 2)
  assert.equal(countWords('well-known fact'), 3)
  assert.equal(countWords('room 101 and 7'), 4)
  assert.equal(countWords('café crème'), 2)
})

test('countWords throws TypeError for non-string input', () => {
  assert.throws(() => countWords(42), TypeError)
  assert.throws(() => countWords(null), TypeError)
})
EOF
npm test 2>&1 | grep -E "^ℹ (pass|fail)"
